A1-discharge-nstemi.documentText:
Manchester Royal Infirmary - Cardiology Ward 7
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Mr David Okafor   NHS No: 943 476 5919   DOB: 14/03/1961
Admitted: 11/11/2026   Discharged: 15/11/2026
Consultant: Dr R. Patel

Diagnosis: Non-ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI)
Procedure: Coronary angiogram 12/11/2026 - 1 x drug-eluting stent to the left anterior descending artery (LAD).
Echocardiogram: Mildly impaired left ventricular function, ejection fraction 45%.

Medications on discharge:
Aspirin 75 mg once daily - continue lifelong (NEW)
Ticagrelor 90 mg twice daily - for 12 months, then stop (NEW)
Atorvastatin 80 mg once daily at night (NEW)
Bisoprolol 2.5 mg once daily (NEW)
Ramipril 2.5 mg once daily (NEW)
GTN spray 400 micrograms - 1-2 sprays under the tongue for chest pain, may repeat after 5 minutes (NEW)

Medications stopped: Ibuprofen 400 mg - STOP. Do not take ibuprofen or other anti-inflammatory painkillers.

Advice to patient: If you have chest pain lasting more than 15 minutes despite using your GTN spray, call 999 immediately. Do not drive for 1 week. Do not stop ticagrelor without speaking to the cardiology team.

Follow-up:
1. GP to check kidney function and potassium (U&E) in 2 weeks after starting ramipril.
2. Cardiac rehabilitation team will contact you within 4 weeks.
3. Cardiology outpatient clinic in 3 months.

Anticoagulation Clinic - Warfarin Dosing Record
North Tees and Hartlepool NHS Foundation Trust
Patient: Mrs Joan Price   DOB 30/01/1944
Indication: Atrial fibrillation   Target INR range: 2.0 - 3.0
Tablets: 1 mg (brown), 3 mg (blue), 5 mg (pink)

INR today (20/11/2026): 4.6
Previous dose: 4 mg daily

New dosing instructions:
Thursday 20/11/2026 - OMIT (take no warfarin)
Friday 21/11/2026 - OMIT (take no warfarin)
From Saturday 22/11/2026 - 3 mg daily (one blue tablet)

Next INR test: Tuesday 25/11/2026 at 10:15, Hartlepool clinic room 4.

If you notice any bleeding that will not stop, blood in your urine or black stools, a severe headache, or you have a fall and hit your head, go to A&E straight away and take your yellow book.

analysis.title: Warfarin dose change after a high INR reading
analysis.summary: Your clinic says to skip warfarin on Thursday and Friday, then take 3 mg (one blue tablet) every day from Saturday.
analysis.plainEnglish: Your blood test today showed your blood is thinner than the clinic wants, so they paused your warfarin for two days. From Saturday 22 November you start one blue 3 mg tablet daily, instead of the 4 mg you were taking. You have another blood test booked for Tuesday 25 November at 10:15.
sourceAnchors: From Saturday 22/11/2026 - 3 mg daily (one blue tablet)
Next INR test: Tuesday 25/11/2026 at 10:15, Hartlepool clinic room 4.

keyPoints.detail: The record says to take none on Thursday 20 November and none on Friday 21 November.

keyPoints.label: Then one blue tablet a day
keyPoints.detail: From Saturday 22 November you take 3 mg daily, which is a single blue tablet.
keyPoints.sourceAnchor: From Saturday 22/11/2026 - 3 mg daily (one blue tablet)

keyPoints.label: This is a drop from your old dose
keyPoints.detail: You were taking 4 mg daily before; the new plan is 3 mg daily.

keyPoints.label: Your blood test came back high
keyPoints.detail: Today's INR was 4.6, above the 2.0 to 3.0 range the clinic is aiming for. A higher number means the blood is taking longer to clot.

keyPoints.label: Another test is already booked
keyPoints.detail: Tuesday 25 November at 10:15 in Hartlepool clinic room 4.
keyPoints.sourceAnchor: Next INR test: Tuesday 25/11/2026 at 10:15, Hartlepool clinic room 4.

keyPoints.detail: The record lists the reason as atrial fibrillation, an irregular heartbeat.

metrics.label: Today's INR
metrics.caveat: Above the 2.0-3.0 range the clinic is aiming for.

flags.detail: The clinic says to go to A&E straight away if you have bleeding that will not stop, blood in your urine, black stools, a severe headache, or a fall where you hit your head. Take your yellow book with you.

questions: If I accidentally took a tablet on Thursday or Friday, what should I do?

nextActions: Write the plan somewhere you'll see it: none Thursday, none Friday, one blue 3 mg tablet daily from Saturday.
Check you have enough 3 mg blue tablets at home before Saturday.
Put the Tuesday 25 November 10:15 appointment in your diary and plan how you'll get to Hartlepool clinic room 4.
Keep your yellow anticoagulant book with you when you go out.
Ring the anticoagulation clinic if anything about the dose is unclear.
analysis.safetyNote: Your clinic has already spotted the high reading and given you a clear plan, and they'll recheck your blood on Tuesday.

A10-methotrexate-weekly.question: Can you confirm how and when I should take each medicine?
A10-methotrexate-weekly.documentText:
Department of Rheumatology, Royal Derby Hospital
Date: 10/11/2026
To: Dr M. Ali, Ashbourne Road Surgery
Re: Mr Peter Lomax, DOB 05/05/1972

Diagnosis: Rheumatoid arthritis (seropositive).

I have started Mr Lomax on methotrexate.
- Methotrexate 15 mg (six 2.5 mg tablets) ONCE A WEEK, taken on Mondays. Not to be taken daily.
- Folic acid 5 mg ONCE A WEEK, taken on Thursdays (not on the same day as methotrexate).
- Prednisolone 10 mg once daily for 2 weeks, then 5 mg once daily for 2 weeks, then stop.

Monitoring: FBC, U&E and LFTs every 2 weeks for 6 weeks, then monthly for 3 months.
Please avoid prescribing trimethoprim or co-trimoxazole.
I have advised Mr Lomax to contact us or his GP urgently if he develops a sore throat, fever, mouth ulcers, unexplained bruising or breathlessness. He should limit alcohol to well within national guidance.
Review in rheumatology clinic in 3 months.

Dr J. Fernando, Consultant Rheumatologist

A12-appointment-prep.question: What do I need to do before my appointment?
A12-appointment-prep.documentText:
Endoscopy Unit, Royal Liverpool University Hospital
APPOINTMENT LETTER
Dear Mr Ade Bello,

You have been booked for a GASTROSCOPY (OGD).
Date: Wednesday 2 December 2026
Time: 14:30 - please arrive at 14:00 at Endoscopy Reception, Level 2.

Before your test:
- Do not eat anything for 6 hours before your appointment. You may drink sips of water up to 2 hours before.
- Stop omeprazole 2 weeks before your test (from 18/11/2026) unless your doctor told you not to.
- If you take metformin, do not take your morning dose on the day of the test.
- Bring a list of your current medicines.
- If you choose sedation, an adult must collect you and stay with you for 12 hours. You must not drive for 24 hours.

If you cannot attend, please call 0151 706 2000 ext. 4471 at least 48 hours before so the slot can be offered to someone else.
